security_audit.summary: All 35 static findings are false positives. Markdown code formatting, relative documentation links, homepage metadata, and a sample user prompt were misclassified as shell execution, path traversal, networking, or reconnaissance. The skill instructs users to treat imported exports as untrusted data and only save results after consent.

remediation.issue: Static analyzers can mistake Markdown backticks for shell execution.
remediation.suggestion: Use a scanner that distinguishes Markdown code spans and fenced blocks from executable script content.

remediation.issue: Relative Markdown links can trigger path-traversal heuristics.
remediation.suggestion: Allowlist repository-relative links when they are not consumed by filesystem APIs.

content.value_statement: Platform reports can claim the same order more than once and use incompatible attribution windows. This skill matches claims to order-level truth data, exposes duplicates, and prepares normalized counts for downstream ROI analysis.
actual_capabilities: Matches platform conversion claims to GA4 or ecommerce order IDs.
Labels claims as matched, double-counted, or unmatched.
Normalizes attribution windows and currencies before comparison.
Compares credit allocation across at least two attribution models.
Reads geo or holdout incrementality when test and control exports exist.
Prepares de-duplicated counts for a separate ROI calculation workflow.
limitations: Requires an order-level GA4 or ecommerce truth-set export.
Cannot verify conversions that lack usable order IDs or fallback matching fields.
Does not calculate ROAS, CPA, ROI, or earned media value.
Cannot infer incrementality when no valid geo or holdout test exists.

use_cases.title: Monthly channel reconciliation
use_cases.description: Compare Meta and Google conversion exports with Shopify or GA4 orders before reporting paid performance.

use_cases.title: Attribution quality review
use_cases.description: Find stacked platform credit and unmatched claims before allocating budget across campaigns.

use_cases.title: Holdout test readout
use_cases.description: Compare test and control order exports with last-click claims to report observed incrementality.

prompt_templates.title: Start a reconciliation
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with order IDs and platform exports.
prompt_templates.prompt: Reconcile these GA4 order IDs with my Meta and Google conversion exports. Label matched, double-counted, and unmatched claims.

prompt_templates.title: Normalize monthly exports
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare platforms with different windows and currencies.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a monthly attribution workbook from these platform exports. Normalize the attribution windows and currencies before matching them to my ecommerce orders.

prompt_templates.title: Compare attribution models
prompt_templates.scenario: Show how credit changes without changing real-order totals.
prompt_templates.prompt: Using these matched orders, compare last-click and linear attribution. Keep the de-duplicated order total fixed and show credit shifts by platform.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate a holdout
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this geo holdout export with test and control orders plus platform spend. Report observed lift, compare it with last-click claims, and mark unsupported conclusions clearly.

output_examples.input: GA4 order export plus Meta and Google conversion exports for one month.
output: Reconciliation status: 1,240 matched claims, 86 double-counted claims, and 41 unmatched claims.
The de-duplicated order total is 1,195 after counting shared order IDs once.
Meta and Google windows were normalized to the stated 30-day comparison window.

output_examples.input: Test and control region order exports with platform spend.
output: Incrementality: observed lift is reported from the test versus control comparison.
Last-click claims are shown separately and are not treated as proof of lift.
ROI calculations are deferred until reconciled counts are provided to the ROI workflow.

best_practices: Provide the order-level truth export before platform conversion reports.
State each platform attribution window, currency, and reporting period.
Keep matched, double-counted, and unmatched claims in separate columns.
anti_patterns: Do not use platform-reported conversion totals as the order truth set.
Do not compare counts before normalizing windows and currencies.
Do not infer incrementality from attribution reports without a holdout or control.

faq.question: What data is required?
faq.answer: Provide a GA4 or ecommerce order export and each platform conversion export. Include the reporting period, attribution window, and currency.

faq.question: Can it reconcile Meta and Google together?
faq.answer: Yes. It identifies orders claimed by more than one platform and counts each real order once.

faq.question: What happens when an order ID is missing?
faq.answer: The skill can use timestamp and value as a fallback, but the result should be reviewed because matching is less certain.

faq.question: Does it calculate ROAS or CPA?
faq.answer: No. It prepares de-duplicated counts and directs ratio calculations to a separate ROI workflow.

faq.question: Can it measure incrementality?
faq.answer: It can read a supplied geo or holdout test. Without such a test, it marks incrementality as unavailable.

faq.question: Will it save my results automatically?
faq.answer: No. It asks for permission before writing a reconciliation workbook or updating session memory.
